rows.label: Lethality threshold, primary blast (lung)
rows.source_ref: UFC 3-340-02 1-11.1 Table 1-1: lethality threshold 100-120 psi maximum effective pressure, 3-5 ms
rows.note: Metric is MAXIMUM EFFECTIVE pressure (incident, incident + dynamic, or reflected, whichever is highest), not incident. For a person standing in the open use Ps + q; against a wall use Pr. For long durations (gas explosions) UFC says lung thresholds fall to about one third.

alternatives.basis: UFC Table 1-1 lethality 50 % (130 psi lower end)
IOGP 434-14 offshore consensus: fatality threshold about 0.2 bar when debris, impact and structures dominate
IOGP 434-14: UK HSE probit gives 1 % lethality at about 0.35 bar (long-duration blasts)

sources.quoted_phrase: Table 1-1 Blast Effects In Man Applicable To Fast-Rising Air Blasts Of Short Duration (3-5 ms)
Maximum effective pressure is the highest of incident pressure, incident pressure plus dynamic pressure, or reflected pressure.
the threshold for lethality due to lung damage is approximately 100 to 120 psi
